note: READINGS THIS ARCHIVE HAS WITHDRAWN, and which must not be stated as fact anywhere in its data. Checked by the kit's checkretired.py, designed in the Falco archive. The rule that makes it work: a retired phrase is THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN WORDING, never a document's, so an unquoted hit is a claim and a quoted one is a quotation. A retired SURNAME could not be checked this way — the documents contain it.
markNote: This archive quotes a dead reading in curly double quotes, as its corrections register already does; guillemets are accepted too because the kit's tool was written against an archive that uses them.

phrases.why: The live domain has no dot in it — nationalarchives.gov.za. The host as published has no address record and no mail record at all, so a reader following it reached nothing.
Withdrawn six hours after publishing. Martha Angeline Kolbe's stone is in WAKKERSTROOM MAIN CEMETERY. The index gave the district, not the grave, and the archive read a concentration camp into it.
A different farm of the same name. The Friend of the Free State, 13 January 1870, puts the Kolbe Leeuberg elsewhere.

skipNote: NO FILE IS EXEMPT, AND ONE WAS FOR AN HOUR. This archive first exempted /searched/ and the work list on the ground that a dated log records what was believed then and must not be edited now. **The Falco session, whose design this is, pushed back and was right.** The test is not *is this a log*, it is *would a reader act on this row today* — and a searched register is acted on precisely so nobody repeats a search, so exempting it removes the check from the page that most needs it. **The third option is the one both archives already use elsewhere: keep the withdrawn text and put the correction in the same row.** The history stays, the reader cannot act on the dead half, and the phrase is no longer stated as fact, which is the only thing this gate tests.
